title: Nārāyaṇa in the disc of the Sun

words.meaning: dwelling in the centre of the disc of the Sun
holding the conch and the discus

samasa.meaning: who abides in the middle of the Sun’s disc
by whom conch and discus are held

morphology.note: sarasija ‘born in the lake’ is a lotus (an aluk compound: the locative sarasi is kept).

translation.literal: To be meditated on always is Nārāyaṇa dwelling in the middle of the Sun’s disc, seated on a lotus seat, with armlets, with makara earrings, crowned, garlanded, golden-bodied, holding conch and discus.
translation.readable: Meditate always on Nārāyaṇa in the heart of the Sun’s disc: seated on a lotus, wearing armlets, makara earrings, a crown and a necklace, his body golden, the conch and discus in his hands.

meaning: A meditation verse that places Nārāyaṇa at the centre of the Sun’s disc and describes him piece by piece: the lotus seat, the ornaments (armlets, earrings shaped like the makara, crown, necklace), the golden body, and the conch and discus in his hands. It follows namaḥ savitre and makes the same identification visible: the Sun that has been worshipped all through the rite is to be seen with Nārāyaṇa within it.
in_the_rite: Step sūrya-nārāyaṇa-vandana, all three services, after namaḥ savitre.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Vasantatilakā metre: four pādas of fourteen syllables. M writes वपुः धृत- unjoined (corrections.json).
